spec: DESIGN.md — installations, the machine seam, standalone savestate cards (issue #225)
description: Whole fixture machines in; the canonical SavestatePlacement serialization (atlas/contract.py) out, asserted with exact equality — for catalogue entries whose launch command names a standalone emulator a packaged savestate card covers (atlas/data/standalone_savestates.json). The card states where the states tree hangs and how the emulator names a state; the resolver reads the emulator's own configuration the way the emulator does, at the revision the arrangement ships. Root kind is emulator_directory (or the ROM's own directory / the launch's cwd for melonDS's empty and relative values): no frontend hands these emulators a state root. Un-carded emulators keep the standalone-unsupported refusal byte-identically.

vectors.name: retrodeck-dolphins-states-tree-is-the-compiled-join
vectors.rationale: Dolphin's states tree is a compiled join no configuration moves — <user dir>/StateSaves (FileUtil.cpp:852, CommonPaths.h:59 at 2603a) — so the answer reads no file at all: the emulator's own data tree below the flatpak-pinned XDG base, the StateSaves segment, and the cited naming pattern (<game_id>.s<slot>) in the file-names-unestablished caveat, because a game id is nothing a content path derives. The file set stays unknown: nothing here can list states nobody can name.

vectors.rationale: RPCS3's saves hang off the emulated drive vfs.yml routes; its states never touch it — fs::get_config_dir() + savestates/ + <title>/ is a compiled join below the emulator's own config directory (savestate_utils.cpp:293 at 7c6b3dcd), one directory per title. No vfs.yml appears in this fixture and none is needed: the two questions read different sources, which is the point of this vector.

vectors.name: retrodeck-pcsx2s-written-savestates-line-governs-despite-its-spelling
vectors.rationale: The issue's own trap: RetroDECK writes the key spelled SaveStates (components/pcsx2/component_prepare.sh:25) while the source reads "Savestates" (Pcsx2Config.cpp:2284 at v2.6.3). SimpleIni matches keys ASCII case-insensitively (CSimpleIniA over SI_GenericNoCase, SimpleIni.h:3642-3643, :2916-2931), so the written line IS the key and its directory governs — answering the compiled sstates default here would be reading the file some other way than the emulator does.

vectors.name: an-uncarded-standalone-entry-refuses-exactly-as-before
vectors.rationale: XRoar carries no savestate card — its snapshot feature is real, but a snapshot lands wherever the save dialog's user points it (xroar.c:2320-2325 at 1.10), a statement no shape of this family makes yet — so the refusal is byte-identical to what every standalone entry answered before the family landed: standalone-unsupported with the label and system. An absent card must never read as a smaller absence. (This pin sat on xemu until #284 carded it.)

vectors.name: emudeck-an-uncarded-token-refuses-on-this-route-too
vectors.rationale: EmuDeck's entry route runs its own dispatch (launch identity, then the card), and this pins its no-card branch: XRoar's %EMULATOR_XROAR% token identifies a launch and no savestate card covers the emulator, so the refusal is the same standalone-unsupported, byte-identical to the pre-family answer. (This pin sat on xemu until #284 carded it.)

vectors.name: emudeck-duckstation-writes-the-states-key-itself
vectors.rationale: EmuDeck writes SaveStates = <its states tree> into settings.ini (emuDeckDuckStation.sh:67-75), so the configured value governs — read through the same two-base DataRoot probe as the save answer, here answering from the data side an AppImage launch without XDG_CONFIG_HOME reads.

vectors.name: emudeck-the-w-flag-forces-the-proton-variant-which-refuses-the-states-too
vectors.rationale: duckstation.sh -w runs the Windows build under Proton, whose configuration lives inside the Proton prefix and is not read — the same variant gate the save answer runs, refusing with the variant named rather than answering from a Linux config this launch never opens.

vectors.name: emudeck-melonds-states-answer-from-the-flatpaks-own-homes

vectors.name: retrodeck-a-carded-no-answers-the-states-question-for-cemu
vectors.rationale: Cemu 2.6 has no savestates — no state serializer anywhere in the v2.6 tree, none in the shipped binary's unfiltered scan, and the project's own issue template lists 'Add savestates' among features yet to be implemented — and #284 makes that an ANSWER: no_savestates with the card's citation, not the generic standalone-unsupported refusal. No machine-derived caveats ride it; the statement is about the emulator, not about this machine.

no_savestates.citation: Cemu 2.6: unfiltered strings scan of the shipped components/cemu/bin/Cemu_relwithdebinfo carries no savestate or snapshot vocabulary, and the v2.6 tree's only 'savestate' spellings are the graphic-packs window persisting its own UI state (src/gui/GraphicPacksWindow2.cpp:326) and the issue template listing 'Add savestates' among features yet to be implemented (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_report.yaml:18)

vectors.name: an-unpinned-build-rides-the-stated-no-as-unverified-version

The stated no answers anyway, before the gate: the absence is a fact about the emulator generation, not about which of its builds a launch would pick, so refusing it over an unestablished variant would withhold an answer the question has.

vectors.name: retrodeck-xemus-snapshots-live-inside-the-hard-disk-image
vectors.rationale: xemu's savestates are QEMU internal snapshots written into the qcow2 that [sys.files] hdd_path names — the vmstate into the image, the record across every snapshot-capable device, of which that image is the only one (savevm.c:3285-3301, block/snapshot.c:736-777 at v0.8.135), and xemu's own snapshot browser opens exactly that file to list them (xemu-snapshots.c:156-158). So the answer names the image the way the save answer does, and savestate-inside-image is what keeps 'here is the file' from reading as 'and states lie beside it'. The config-home toml is reached through RetroDECK's own symlink, walked like any other.

vectors.name: xemu-no-disk-image-means-no-snapshot-store
vectors.rationale: A machine with no hard-disk image configured cannot snapshot at all — QEMU refuses with 'no block device can store vmstate for snapshot' (block/snapshot.c:779-781 at v0.8.135) — so the answer refuses with the fact named instead of inventing a directory: emulator-config-unreadable, the same code the save answer uses where nothing its configuration names can anchor an answer.

vectors.name: emudeck-xemus-snapshots-answer-from-the-flatpaks-own-toml
vectors.rationale: On EmuDeck the launch runs the app.xemu.xemu flatpak the save card records, so the savestate answer reads the app's own xemu.toml below ~/.var/app and names the image it points at — the same inside-the-image statement as on RetroDECK, reached through the variant gate the save answer shares.
